description: ONE PROMISE IN A CONTRACT, and the amount of the transaction price allocated to it. ASC 606 recognises revenue when control of a distinct good or service transfers — so the unit of recognition is the obligation, not the contract and not the invoice. A contract to grow, pack and ship is three obligations that are satisfied on three different days, and a system that recognised the whole contract on the first of them would be wrong for the whole gap between them.

fields.description: What was promised, in the words of the contract — 'Deliver 4,000 bins of Gala', 'Provide controlled-atmosphere storage through March'.
fields.label: Obligation

fields.description: The share of the contract's transaction price allocated to this promise. ASC 606-10-32-31 allocates on relative standalone selling price; this app stores what somebody allocated and checks that the parts sum to the whole — it does not compute the allocation, because a standalone selling price is a judgement about a market and not an arithmetic operation on a contract.
fields.label: Allocated

fields.description: Whether control has transferred. THE FIELD THE `revenue_recognition` CONTROL READS: recognising against an unsatisfied obligation is reported (Advisory) or refused (Enforced).
fields.label: Satisfied

fields.description: What shows control transferred — a scale ticket, a bill of lading, a settlement statement. The date says when somebody claims it happened; this says how anybody else could check.
fields.label: Evidence

name: Revenue Performance Obligation
